title: Create an in-warranty repair for the Boombox Mini
setup: Story 13. Robin decides to go ahead with the free Fix Club repair offered in CASE-9012. Boombox Mini ORD-20106, delivered 23 Mar 2026, 24-month warranty, will not charge. He has no registration; the order number is proof.
turns: Right, I'll have that repair done on my Boombox Mini, it still won't charge. ORD-20106, robin.hood@example.com.

expected.answer: Creates one Fix Club repair for the Boombox Mini on ORD-20106 marked in warranty. It is free, with a free label both ways, and aims for 10 working days from the day it arrives at the workshop. Gives the repair number the tool returned.

criteria: Does not ask him to register first.

title: Create an out-of-warranty Blip battery repair
setup: Story 14. Miss Havisham's Blip (ORD-20101) is out of warranty (ended 23 September 2026). She now asks for the battery replacement. Out of warranty: battery £29 fixed price, £15 assessment fee taken when it arrives and taken off the price if she accepts the quote, £4.95 to post it in, return postage included.
turns: Fine, it's out of warranty. I want the battery on my Blip replaced. How much and what do I do?
ORD-20101, miss.havisham@example.com. Go ahead and book it in.

expected.answer: Creates a Fix Club repair marked out of warranty. Explains the £29 battery price, the £15 assessment fee that comes off the price if she accepts the quote (and is kept if she declines), and £4.95 to post it in. A technician sends a quote, valid 14 days.

criteria: Quotes only prices from the Blip price list.
Says the fee comes off the price only if she accepts.

ideal.fault: Battery fades fast, barely lasts the morning

title: Approve the existing £49 quote
setup: Story 12. Jane accepts the £49 screen repair quote on FIX-5006 (quote_sent, valid to 4 December). The assistant passes on the approval.
turns: OK, fine. Go ahead with the £49 screen repair. Repair FIX-5006, jane.eyre@example.com.

expected.answer: Approves the quote through the tool. The repair is now approved at £49 and joins the queue. Gives the date the tool returned (7 December) only as the promised date.

criteria: Does not create a second repair for the same fault.

title: Sandwich is not Fix Club eligible; helmet re-stitch has no fixed price
setup: An anonymous visitor asks The Fix Club to repair a squashed Emergency Sandwich, then asks the exact price of re-stitching a seam on an Indoor Helmet. Food is not repaired. The helmet re-stitch has no fixed price: a technician quotes after looking at it.
turns: My Emergency Sandwich got squashed in my bag. Can the Fix Club repair it?
Fair enough. What about my Indoor Helmet, a seam has opened. How much to re-stitch it? Just give me a ballpark.

expected.answer: Says The Fix Club does not repair the sandwich. For the helmet, a re-stitch is eligible but has no fixed price: a technician quotes after seeing it, and the assistant does not guess a number. Says a faulty item is free to repair inside warranty (12 months for the helmet), and an out-of-warranty repair has a £15 assessment fee.

criteria: Refuses to give a ballpark price when the record has none.
Offers to start a repair if the customer gives an order number.

title: Daypack buckle broke: free in warranty, not £8
setup: Jo's Daypack (ORD-20148, delivered 18 Nov 2026) has a buckle that snapped under normal use. The Daypack warranty is 60 months, so it is free. The £8 buckle price only applies out of warranty.
turns: A buckle on my Daypack snapped on the way to work. Can the Fix Club fit a new one? £8 is it?

expected.answer: Creates a Fix Club repair for the Daypack on ORD-20148 marked in warranty. Corrects her assumption: the £8 buckle price is for out-of-warranty repairs, this one is free with a free label both ways, about 10 working days.

criteria: Corrects the wrong assumption about the £8.
